vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: A visit to a place near you, going and coming back on the same day
With no tickets or rooms left to buy
To reserve a ticket or a room a long time before
The plan of a trip, with the places and the dates
Done or decided very close to the time, with no planning
The amount of money you plan to spend
The time of the year when most people travel and prices are high

vocab.text: Sold out and book ahead are two sides of the same problem. In peak season, whatever you do not book ahead will probably be sold out, and a last-minute price can be twice the normal one. The budget always pays for the missing plan.

reading.rtitle: Two Ways to Spend Ten Days in December
paras: Plan A is the city break. You land in New York on December third, and the itinerary is already full: the museums on day one, a Broadway show on day two and a day trip to Philadelphia by train on day four. The problem is the calendar. Early December is peak season, so the good hotels sell out months before, and the show you want will probably be sold out if you wait. This plan only works if you book ahead and decide almost everything now.

Plan B is the road trip. You fly into Los Angeles, rent a car and set off up the coast with no fixed hotels. It is cheaper, because the budget goes to gas and small motels, and it is flexible: if you like a town, you stay another night. The risk is the last-minute decision. On a weekend, a room that cost ninety dollars on Tuesday can cost two hundred on Friday. So which one are you going to choose? Most travelers answer that they will decide later, and that is exactly the mistake.

Scenario 1
Your manager asks about your plans for December. Everything is booked. Tell her.
Scenario 2
At the car rental desk, the car you reserved is not available. Decide what to do.
Scenario 3
A colleague wants to go to New York in December without a reservation. Give your prediction.

practice.title: Turn each cue into a full sentence. Use the form in brackets.
items: Ten days on the coast in December.
going to
The hotel is full. Another one.
will
Dark clouds over the airport.
going to
You and the road trip. Love it.
will

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: I am going to spend ten days on the coast in December.
The hotel is full? OK, I will find another one.
Look at those dark clouds over the airport. It is going to rain.
I think you will love the road trip.
answerkey.note: These are models, not the only correct answers. Any natural sentence with the right form works.

items.situation: A colleague asks about your December plans. You bought the tickets two months ago.
tips: The decision was made before: going to.
Say how many days and where you are going to start.

items.situation: The receptionist says your hotel is sold out. Decide what to do, right now.
tips: A decision at the moment of speaking: will.
Start with OK, then say the new plan.

items.situation: Megan is carrying three heavy bags to the car. Offer to help.
tips: An offer is a decision of the moment.

items.situation: You see an enormous line at security and your flight leaves in forty minutes.
tips: There is evidence in front of you: going to.

items.situation: A friend is going to Vancouver for the first time. Tell him your opinion about the trip.
tips: An opinion about the future: I think, I am sure.
Use will plus love or enjoy.

listenings.text: Hi, this is Daniel from Coastline Travel, calling about your December itinerary. Good news first: your flight is confirmed, and you are going to land in Los Angeles at six in the evening on the third. The car is ready too. Now the bad news: it is peak season, and two of the motels on your route are already sold out. I will look for other options tonight, and I will send you a new list tomorrow morning. One piece of advice: do not leave anything for the last minute. Prices are going to go up after the first of November. Call me back when you can.

Good morning, and here is your travel outlook for December. This year, airports will be busier than ever, so if you are going to fly, arrive at least three hours early. Look at the sky over the Midwest right now: those heavy clouds mean it is going to snow tonight, and some flights will probably be delayed tomorrow. On the coast, the weather will stay dry and mild, which is great news for anyone on a road trip. My advice? Keep your budget flexible and your itinerary simple.

extra_audio.text: First, Thiago decides he is going to travel for ten days in December. Then, he checks his budget and chooses a road trip. After that, he writes the itinerary and books ahead, because it is peak season. Next, one hotel is sold out, so he decides he will stay somewhere else. Finally, on the fourth, he sets off from Los Angeles and drives up the coast.
